items.text: Merrill Lynch created two new kinds of fees for third-party asset managers: data analytics fees and a negotiable revenue-sharing 'support fee,' effective Jan. 1, 2027.
items.quote: Two kinds of fees have been newly created. Third-party managers can buy as much as $1.4 million worth of “incentives” per annum through one fee, by maxing out data analytics buys. ... effective, Jan. 1, 2027.

items.text: Merrill's new data analytics fees will cost asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per firm, per year for data on actively managed products.
items.quote: Merrill's new data analytics fees will cost asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per-firm, per-year for data on actively managed products, including ETFs, mutual funds, annuities and model portfolios.

items.text: Merrill's new 'negotiable' revenue-sharing 'support fee' will cost up to $1 million for every $1 billion of funds an asset manager manages on behalf of Merrill advisors.
items.quote: Its new “negotiable” revenue-sharing “support fee” will cost up to $1 million, for every $1 billion of funds an asset manager manages on behalf of Merrill advisors

items.text: Merrill announced the launch of Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), new services available through the Merrill Lynch Investment Advisory Program.
items.quote: Merrill today announced the launch of Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), new services that combine automation with professional portfolio oversight

items.text: Merrill agreed to pay $39 million to settle a class action lawsuit alleging it paid brokerage clients close-to-zero interest rates instead of market rates on cash in retirement accounts.
items.quote: agreeing this week to pay $39 million to settle a class action lawsuit that alleged it paid brokerage clients close-to-zero interest rates instead of market rates on cash in retirement accounts

items.text: Merrill Lynch faces restitution of approximately $549,000 in excess commissions as part of a combined $4.4 million settlement with Wells Fargo over unreasonable commissions on small-dollar retail equity transactions.
items.quote: Merrill Lynch faces restitution on approximately $549,000 in excess commissions over the same period

items.text: Bank of America (Merrill) had a net loss of 552 advisors this year through Aug. 13, the largest net loss among advisors, according to Wolfe Research.
items.quote: Bank of America had a net loss of 552 advisors, followed by Edward Jones and Equitable Advisors, with 334 each.

items.text: Merrill executives touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting after largely pulling back in 2017.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting.

items.text: Merrill Lynch client sales of alternative investments increased 19% in the third quarter, per president and co-head Eric Schimpf, and the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities.
items.quote: At Merrill Lynch, client sales of alternative investments increased 19% in the quarter, said Eric Schimpf, president and co-head of Merrill Wealth Management

items.text: GWIM client balances climbed above $5 trillion for the first time, up 9%, with quarterly net client flows of about $38 billion.
items.quote: Client balances climbed above $5 trillion for the first time, up 9%, while AUM rose 12% to about $2.4 trillion. Quarterly net client flows were about $38 billion

items.text: Merrill's co-presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer, returning the firm to veteran broker recruiting.
items.quote: The firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.
